simple.meaning: אַנְתָּה (ʼantâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “thou.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 25 times across Ezra, Daniel, beginning at Ezra 7:25. Its contexts include Torah, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַנְתָּה (H607).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: אַנְתָּה (ʼantâh) / H607 is traced through Ezra 7:25, Daniel 2:29, Daniel 2:31, Daniel 2:37 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: You, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your God that is in your hand, appoint magistrates and judges, who may judge all the people who are beyond the River, who all know the laws of your God; and teach him who doesn’t know them.

“As for you, O king, your thoughts came on your bed, what should happen hereafter; and he who reveals secrets has made known to you what will happen.

You, O king, are king of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given the kingdom, the power, the strength, and the glory.

definitions.full: H607. antah אנתה Kt 14 (i.e. אַנְתָּה , peculiar to Biblical Aramaic; Qr אַנְתְּ ) pronoun 2 masculine singular thou (Biblical Hebrew אַתָּה ; Cappadocian and Egyptian Aramaic אנת (Lab Eph. 1. 67 ; S-C A 11 +, feminine אנתי ib. D9, 11, 26+), Nerab את (Cooke 186. 190 ), Palmyrene אנת ( ib. 308); ᵑ7 Onk ᵑ7 את, J אנת ( § 16. 1 ); Syriac ); — thou , Dan 2:29 , 31 , 37 , 38 etc., Ezra 7:25 .
